🚀 weft-loom | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Creating and performing algorithmic music through a visual interface that is directly linked to code.
✨ Key Features: • Visual music creation with step grids and piano rolls linked to Strudel code • Sound browser for selecting, recording, and importing sounds • Song panel for arranging patterns and creating variations • Live performance features with keyboard input
📖 Summary: Weft Loom is a free, open-source desktop application for creating pattern-based music using Strudel. It offers a visual interface with step grids and piano rolls that directly correspond to and can rewrite the underlying Strudel code, allowing users to create music without extensive coding or to easily modify existing code.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 De-Nox | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: Cleaning up disk space occupied by build artifacts and dependencies of inactive software projects without accidentally deleting files from active projects.
✨ Key Features: • Intelligent disk cleanup based on project activity, not just artifact age • Terminal-based TUI using ratatui • Read-only until explicit deletion confirmation • Fast scanning by avoiding deep dives into artifact directories
📖 Summary: De-Nox is a Rust-based terminal disk-cleanup tool that intelligently identifies and removes dormant build artifacts like `node_modules` and `target`. It differentiates between truly abandoned projects and active ones by analyzing the last modification date of the project's source files, not just the artifact directories themselves.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 soundwaves | JavaScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Simulating and visualizing sound wave propagation in 2D environments for acoustic analysis and design.
✨ Key Features: • 2D sound wave simulation • Browser-based interface • Scene drawing and material definition • Planar and axisymmetric modes • Finite element method (FEM) simulation
📖 Summary: SoundWaves is a 2D sound wave simulator that runs in the browser, allowing users to draw scenes, define materials, and simulate wave propagation. It supports both planar and axisymmetric modes, with waves solved using finite elements in Rust compiled to WebAssembly.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 innovation-lab-examples | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To serve as a comprehensive resource and starting point for developers looking to build and experiment with AI agents and multi-agent systems using Python and various popular AI frameworks.
✨ Key Features: • 80+ production-ready AI agent examples • Support for autonomous agents, multi-agent systems, and agentic AI
📖 Summary: This repository provides over 80 production-ready Python examples for building autonomous AI agents, multi-agent systems, and agentic AI workflows. It supports various frameworks and tools like uAgents, LangChain, CrewAI, and major LLMs, catering to beginners and experienced developers alike.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 SoulX-Podcast | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Generating realistic, diverse, and personalized long-form podcast-style audio from text, including multi-speaker dialogues and various paralinguistic expressions.
✨ Key Features: • Long-form, multi-turn, multi-speaker dialogic speech generation • Cross-dialectal, zero-shot voice cloning • Paralinguistic controls (e.g., laughter, sighs) • Support for Mandarin, English, and several Chinese dialects (Sichuanese, Henanese, Cantonese)
📖 Summary: SoulX-Podcast is a Python-based inference codebase for generating high-fidelity, long-form podcasts from text. It supports multi-turn, multi-speaker dialogic speech generation, cross-dialectal voice cloning, and paralinguistic controls for enhanced realism.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source
